result_text:
`all_files.zip` now looks up and names its five scope entries from the configured aspect names, so renaming an aspect no longer breaks the export. The `reports` module compiles. The `-Dtest='DataExport*'` run printed nothing, and I didn't check whether any test class matches that pattern. I didn't write a test for the renamed case or run it with a renamed aspect.

The change is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, in the zip-building block near the end of the data export. It replaces the five hard-coded `aspect_*.txt` literals with a loop over the main, test, generated, build-and-deployment and other aspects. Each file name comes from `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call that writes the loose text files.

With the default configuration the entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` and `aspect_other.txt`, in that order. With the renamed aspect, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`. The failure that used to skip `all_files.zip` and `git-history.zip` can no longer happen for this reason, so `git-history.zip` is written again whenever a `git-history.txt` exists.

I left the literal `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` in `LandscapeAnalyzer.java:283` alone. It reads other repositories' reports, which is outside this task.
